messages:
Maria (security): Quick Q — before we sign off on the partner SIEM ingestion, can we align on log residency, retention tiers, and who can request historical unwrapped exports?
Maria (security): TL;DR: partner wants 1-year retention window for some signals, legal asked about PII, and the integrator wants an API to pull historic batches.
Ken (eng-infra): @Maria — we should avoid handing out long-lived unwrap permissions. Pattern that works: encrypted export objects (S3) + envelope keys in KMS. If partner needs historic pulls, create timeboxed grants and require a ticket for each pull.
Ken (eng-infra): Example grant flow we use elsewhere: create a short-lived grant via KMS and return a temporary credential to the exporter. No human should have direct Decrypt perms.
Ken (eng-infra): snippet:```sh
# pseudo
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/log-export --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::PARTNER:role/exporter --operations GenerateDataKey --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"export_id":"<id>"}
```
Jamal (oncall): Auditwise: every grant + GenerateDataKey call must emit an event we can tie into pagerduty if it looks anomalous. Also keep export job traces in our observability for 90d so we can replay without unwrapping keys repeatedly.
Sofia (compliance): From a regs perspective: EU logs with user identifiers need data-minimization before an export. For GDPR, 1 year is ok if justified, but prefer 90d default. Any extension must go through legal + evidence of necessity. Also legal-hold overrides lifecycle and must be documented.
Maria (security): Ok, proposed policy draft: retention tiers = [30d, 90d, 365d]. Default = 90d. Partner exports allowed only for 90d unless approved. Exports must be field-filtered (no raw PII) unless explicit legal request. All unwraps require a ticket and two approvers (security + compliance).
Ken (eng-infra): Implementation checklist:
- Create role: `role/siem_exporter` with no direct KMS Decrypt.
- Export service uses GenerateDataKey / Encrypt, stores ciphertext in S3 with tags: residency=us/eu, tier=90d.
- Use KMS grants for temporary unwraps with one-hour TTL.
- Bucket lifecycle: transition->expire based on tier.
YAML sample for enforcement:```yaml
export_policy:
  default_tier: 90d
  allowed_tiers: [30d, 90d, 365d]
  require_approvers: [security, compliance]
  unwrap_ttl: 1h
  residency: [us, eu]
```
Jamal (oncall): +1 on TTL grants. Also add audit-bot to emit `kms.unwrap` events to `security-telemetry` and add a runbook link for suspicious exports.
audit-bot: Recorded event mapping: kms.generate_data_key -> telemetry.event=log_export.kms_gdk, kms.decrypt/grant_use -> telemetry.event=log_export.unwrap.
Sofia (compliance): Add to policy: any export containing user identifiers must be redacted or tokenized; retention extension requests need justification and quarterly review.
Maria (security): I'll capture this as an RFC and open a JIRA: SEC-EXPORTS-42. Action items: Ken to draft grant task automation, Jamal to add alerting and runbook, Sofia to draft redaction checklist, Maria to write approver template. Target: pilot with partner in 3 weeks.
Ken (eng-infra): I'll start a repo with automation and the KMS grant helpers. Will drop a PR for the YAML policy.
Maria (security): Thanks — linking relevant docs here for reference: https://redwood.example/docs/security/log-exports and https://redwood.example/runbooks/export-incident.
Maria (security): Closing thread — will post RFC link once JIRA is created.
